states.content: As of Monday afternoon, family logistics access for Nina Reed is revoked: future appointment details, procedure times, and callback instructions must not be shared with Nina Reed. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival, and that Thursday slot is now specifically a TEE-guided cardioversion case. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Marcus Reed permits use of his cell phone and the patient portal for routine contact, and says the backup line is only for failed reach attempts. His primary contact is his regular cell 617-555-0104, and he asks that any result callbacks use his cell first unless that fails. He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails; the Cedar Bridge front desk stops routing calls after 5 PM, so daytime backup contact through the front desk (617-555-0140) is limited to daytime, and if his cell 617-555-0104 fails after 5 PM the Cedar Bridge evening desk at 617-555-0162 is the after-hours backup number, recorded only as a backup after-hours route. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
